quote.text: Is this all the habit you acquired when you studied philosophy, to look to others and to hope for nothing from yourself and your own acts? Lament therefore and mourn, and when you eat be fearful that you will have nothing to eat to-morrow. Tremble for your wretched slaves, lest they should steal, or run away, or die. Live in this spirit, and never cease to live so, you who never came near philosophy, except in name, and disgraced its principles so far as in you lies, by showing them to be useless and unprofitable to those who take them up.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Recognize that the foundation of nurturing a child lies in your own consistent effort and self-discipline; do not rely solely on external circumstances to define their growth.
    • Instill in your children the virtue of self-reliance by modeling behaviors that emphasize responsibility and proactive improvement, rather than waiting for external providence.
  • Leadership:
    • True leadership demands that you act with integrity and initiative; look first inward to develop the virtues necessary to inspire and guide others.
    • By holding yourself accountable and continually refining your own actions, you transform responsibilities into opportunities for growth, encouraging your team to do the same.
  • Product Management:
    • A product’s success is rooted in a proactive approach—anticipating challenges and acting with purpose rather than depending solely on external feedback or market conditions.
    • Embrace a mindset where continuous improvement and personal accountability shape your decision-making process, ensuring that each act contributes meaningfully to the product’s evolution.
